# HeaderActions unit fixture leaves focus history behind

## Context

While reviewing #21855, Maryam identified another fixture that writes to the FocusManager singleton. The affected test is `test/playwright/unit/tab/HeaderActions.spec.mjs:427`. The hosted failure tracked in #21854 demonstrated a different writer and a different history key.

## The Problem

On `dev` source at `c916b512ee17af5e78c0a27ea547348040c45c47`, the dispatcher test in `test/playwright/unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs:255` passes alone. Run the existing HeaderActions focus-move test before it on one worker with zero retries, and the dispatcher sees `["undefined", "focus-origin"]` where it expects `["focus-origin"]`. This was reproduced locally by copying the otherwise unchanged Focus spec next to HeaderActions under a later filename to force that order.

## The Architectural Reality

`focusOpts` omits `windowId`, so `src/manager/Focus.mjs` records focus enter and move under the `undefined` key. Destroying HeaderActions fixtures leaves that entry in the singleton. `Focus#removeWindow` is the existing scoped cleanup.

## The Fix

The HeaderActions fixture supplies its own window ID to focus enter, move and leave, then removes that exact window in `afterEach`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All HeaderActions tests pass, including the three arms that drive focus enter, move or leave.
- [ ] The same HeaderActions-then-Focus sequence passes on one worker with retries disabled and the unmodified dispatcher assertion.

## Out of Scope

Production focus policy, the Focus dispatcher assertion and the separate Picker fix.
